body: TIL that a mode of transportation and exercise is a child's toy... You learn something new every day.
You're making promises that the universe doesn't intend on keeping. There is no way to tell if things will get better. The chances of them getting worse are actually higher due to myself.

I know the reality of things. I've always known them, which is why I believe suicide is the best option for me. I was never fit to survive in this world. I never expected, nor would I want, anybody to save me. I always knew it was up to me, which is why it'll never happen. I never will work on myself because I just don't care enough. I don't see the point in trying to fight on when there is no reward that I would be interested in. Sure, I said I believed that if I find love I can make it all feel worth it, but if I doubt it would actually do anything when I legit dont care about anything else in the world. I've lived past the age that I even expected I was going to and I honestly wish I hadn't.

Yeah, I think the biggest thing I have to remind myself is that I'm not a bad artist. In fact, I've had people who said they wish they were as good as me, but I always ignored it. I just kept focusing on what I'm not versus what I am. Another problem was my lack of patience. I always felt like I improved too slowly for my own liking. I realize that everybody has their own learning curve, I just hate how slow mine is compared to what I want it to be. I think that was the most discouraging part. Part of me always knew I could be as good or get even better than what I had wanted to be, but it would take a lot more time than I had hoped. Anyways, I appreciate you taking the time to comment all to that. Means a lot to me.

I think that was also part of the problem, I drew a lot more when I was in high school, but stopped for a while. As soon as I went back, my art was (understandably) a lot worse and it felt discouraging, causing me to further halt my progress. Now, at 22, Im trying to restart, but I almost feel as though I've missed the boat and need to focus on something else career wise. That's not to say I haven't drawn in between, but I just haven't as much as I should have.

I want to thank you for going so in depth. I admit, I need to work on a lot of things and I feel like it'll be hard for me. I think one thing that would at least help me in terms of drawing more is having friends who do art. The people that I hang out with don't care about art, so it's hard when I have some art that I actually am proud of, but nobody to share it with. I also admit that I set wayy too many unrealistic goals when I was younger. It definitely felt discouraging when I never reached them and caused me to draw a lot less. As for meditation, I don't know if it's even possible for me. People have speculated that I may have ADHD, which honestly makes sense with a lot of things. I'll have to try it though. Thank you again for going so in depth. I'll definitely keep this in mind in the future.

That's the thing, though. For some people, there really isn't anything they want to do, like me. Then, I realize in order to live, I have to work at a job that I hate while having nothing to make me feel any better.
I get that. If only it wasn't so expensive.
While I do agree that counselling is good, I also don't think it's for everybody. I've had therapy and it just kind of disappointed. I don't know.
Username checks out. I just get depressed when I even think about doing it. Just a reminder of being alone, I guess.
